messages:
sarah_sales: Heads-up — Orion (enterprise finance) is ready to sign a 12-month reserved commit but they want a concrete capacity/runway plan before legal. They expect peak windows at ~600 req/s (burst to ~900) during market open (15m), avg prompt+response ~150 tokens, latency SLO <= 350ms. Need recommended reserved GPU count, autoscale policy suggestions, preheat steps (KV cache warm), and confirmation on how burst credits bill. Also they flagged KMS + AZ spread in the security questionnaire. @marta_eng / @aj_patton can you advise? @olivia_se can you confirm pricing model?

marta_eng: Quick notes — good shape. High-level approach: (1) estimate tokens/s = rps * avg_tokens; (2) map tokens/s to GPUs using bench profiles. For our LLaMA-family 7B on A100 fp16 we typically see ~1500–2000 tokens/s per GPU; quantized INT4/8 drops that to ~700–1200 tokens/s. For 600 sustained rps * 150 tokens => ~90k tokens/s. That arithmetic implies tens of GPUs; exact count depends on model family and quantization. If they need the 350ms tail consistently, favor smaller family (7B/13B) on fp16 or 8-bit instead of pushing a single huge model.

marta_eng: Recommendation (starter plan): reserved pool = 20 GPUs (mixed family, prioritized for lower-latency variants) with autoscale up to 60 GPUs for bursts. Conservative but gives runway for traffic variance and KV cache warmup. Preheat guidance: run KV cache warmup against representative prefix set 10–20 minutes before open.

marta_eng: Example config we use:

```yaml
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 20
  max_replicas: 80
  scale_metric: rps
  scale_target_rps_per_replica: 30
preheat:
  enabled: true
  warmup_minutes: 15
  prompt_set: s3://orion/presets/market_open.json
```

aj_patton: Quick clarifying Qs — what is the traffic mix (short completions vs long generations vs embeddings)? Embeddings and reranking change throughput math. Also we should run a 1-hour smoke with 2x expected concurrency to validate p99 tail.

olivia_se: Pricing notes: reserved commit (12mo) typically gives ~35–40% discount vs list hosted units, plus monthly burst credits allocation. Overage (burst above credits) billed at on-demand rate. Preheat/warmup traffic normally counts toward monthly usage; we can discuss an exclusion clause for contract if legal insists — I'll draft language.

rick_sre: Resilience items — recommend AZ spread across 3 AZs where possible. Add regional fallback policy that routes to a compatible model variant in another region (higher latency but stays available) if eviction/zone outage. Also enable per-route circuit-breaker and health checks in Console.

aj_patton: Can we schedule the POC stress run for next Tue 09:30 PT (market open sim)? Need their workload generator + a sample of real prefixes. We should also capture KV cache hit rates and per-GPU token/s during the run.

sarah_sales: Confirmed — I will ask Orion to provide the generator and a 1-hour sample of prefixes. Also looping legal for preheat exclusion: @olivia_se pls loop in legal and draft the clause.

devops-bot: smoke-test-orion started by marta_eng at 4932100030 — running 30m load at target profile. Logs: https://internal-ci/redwood/orion/smoke-4932100030

marta_eng: Initial results mid-run — control-plane CPU spiking ~70%, p99 latency ~380ms on quantized model. We see good throughput but tail slightly above SLO; next steps: try fp16 variant for critical routes and increase warmup duration. I'll post the run summary when complete.

olivia_se: Drafted pricing appendix and preheat exclusion language, sending to legal and sales separately after this thread.
